title: Memory Leak: Catch the Escaped Objects
concept: A memory leak occurs when you accidentally leave a reference (arrow) to an object you no longer use, preventing GC from cleaning it up.

steps.title: main Method Starts
steps.explanation:
**`public static void main(String[] args)`**

The program's entry point.
We're about to run dangerous code that causes a memory leak.

steps.title: Static List Creation
steps.explanation:
Because of the `static` keyword, this `list` is created when the program starts and stays in memory until the program ends.
Objects stored here are very difficult for GC to collect.
steps.keyInsight: Static variables easily escape GC's watch.
steps.code: static List<Object> list = new ArrayList<>(); // static 변수는 위험해요!

steps.title: Infinite Loop Begins
steps.explanation: Entering an endless loop with `while(true)` that never stops.

steps.title: Mass-Producing Zombie Objects (Memory Leak)
steps.explanation:
With each loop iteration, a 1MB `byte` array is continuously added to the `list`.
Since the list is `static`, it holds onto these objects tightly and never lets go. From GC's perspective, it thinks "they're still being used" and can't discard them.
Eventually the Heap fills up and crashes (OutOfMemoryError).
steps.keyInsight: Leak = not being used but reference isn't broken

quiz.question: What is the most common cause of memory leaks in Java?
options: Using the new keyword too much
Maintaining references to objects that are no longer used
Because the GC algorithm is weak
Because RAM capacity is too small
quiz.explanation:
GC can only clean up Unreachable (unreferenced) objects.
If you keep unused objects in collections, GC cannot intervene.

misconceptions.wrong: Since GC exists, I don't need to worry about freeing memory.
misconceptions.correct: Wrong! You need to make sure to break references to unused objects (set to null) or let them go out of scope.
misconceptions.why: Unintentional reference retention is the main culprit behind leaks.

keyTakeaway: Keep references to a minimum, and be especially careful with static variables!
